[D4:1] Jolene: Hey Deborah! Good to hear from you. How've you been? I've been on an emotional rollercoaster lately, but I'm coping.
[D4:2] Deborah: Hey Jolene! Good to hear from you. All good here - how about you? Anything new happening lately?
[D4:3] Jolene: I had a major milestone last week and it went really well - I'm so relieved and proud. It was a huge accomplishment for me as an engineer.
[D4:4] Deborah: That's awesome. You must have worked really hard for that. I'm so proud of you. Care to share more about it?
[D4:5] Jolene: Thanks so much! I had to plan and research a lot to design and build a sustainable water purifier for a rural community in need. It was tough, but I loved the experience.
[D4:6] Deborah: Your engineering skills really made a difference for people in a rural area. That's amazing! How did it feel when you saw it working?
[D4:7] Jolene: It was such a surreal moment. Seeing it working and providing clean water to the community was incredibly satisfying. It reminded me of how engineering can make a difference in people's lives. It made me feel like I had a purpose and had done something good.
[D4:8] Deborah: So, what are your career aspirations now?
[D4:9] Jolene:  I want to keep working in engineering and continue to make a positive impact on communities in need by creating sustainable solutions. My goal is to contribute towards making the world a better place with my work.
[D4:10] Deborah:  I'm sure great things will keep coming your way. Keep up the good work and follow your passions!
[D4:11] Jolene: Your support means a lot. I'm determined to keep going and make a difference. Your encouragement really motivates me to pursue my passions.
[D4:12] Deborah: When things get tough, just take a deep breath and remember why you're doing this. This is where I spend a lot of my time, teaching yoga. It's a great way to find balance and reconnect with ourselves. I bonded with Anna during yesterday's l yoga class.
[D4:12] Image caption (automatic): a photo of two women in a dance studio doing a dance pose
[D4:13] Jolene: Wow, that's awesome! What new poses did you try?
[D4:14] Deborah: We were trying out different dance poses, like Warrior II, which builds strength and boosts focus.
[D4:14] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman doing a yoga pose on a chair
[D4:15] Jolene: Is it difficult to do?
[D4:16] Deborah: Yes, but this brought us closer to Anna! We supported each other, that means a lot.
[D4:17] Jolene: Can you explain how to do it?
[D4:18] Deborah: Sure! To do this modified pose, sit on the edge of a chair with your feet planted. Twist your torso to one side and use your hand on your knee for support. You'll feel a stretch in your back and shoulders as you hold it for a few breaths, then switch sides. It's great for relaxing tense muscles.
[D4:19] Jolene: Sounds really hard! Here's my bookshelf!
[D4:19] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a book shelf with a lot of books on it
[D4:20] Deborah: That's quite a collection! Have you had a favorite book lately? I'd love to hear your thoughts.
[D4:21] Jolene: Thanks Deborah! I'm really into this book called "Sapiens" - it's a fascinating look at human history and how technology has affected us. It's giving me a lot to think about!
[D4:22] Deborah: Great, this is interesting! Have you come across any recent ones that really struck you?
[D4:23] Jolene: Two weeks ago I read "Avalanche" by Neal Stephenson in one sitting! 
[D4:24] Deborah: That sounds cool, Jolene. Stories can be so powerful - they can teach us, motivate us, and bring us together. 
[D4:25] Jolene: I also read a recent story about someone who became successful despite facing numerous challenges. It really showed me that anything is possible if you believe and work hard.
[D4:26] Deborah: That's a really powerful message. It reminds me of someone special and their grace and strength when they faced hardships. Check out this creation!
[D4:26] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a bouquet of flowers in a vase on a table
[D4:27] Jolene: Wow, Deb! That's beautiful! Can you tell me the backstory of that bouquet?
[D4:28] Deborah: My friend gave me this bouquet when I was struggling, and it gives me hope and courage. I'm filled with warmth and appreciation when I look at it.
[D4:29] Jolene: That's really sweet. Such a small thing can make a real difference.
[D4:30] Deborah: It's amazing how something as simple as flowers can make a real difference. Nature sure is beautiful.
[D4:31] Jolene: Where are some of your favorite nature spots?
[D4:32] Deborah: Oh, there's so many great places! My favorite is a park with a forest trail - it's so calming getting lost in nature. Then there's this beach nearby that I love - the sound of the waves and the sand under my feet make me feel all peaceful and happy. Do you have any favorite spots, Jolene?
[D4:33] Jolene: Here's a picture I took on vacation last summer in Bogota. It was so beautiful and calming watching the sunset over the water. It definitely made me appreciate nature's calming power.
[D4:33] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a person walking on the beach with a surfboard
[D4:34] Deborah: That sounds great, Jolene. Nature's calming for sure. Guess it helps us forget the daily craziness and find inner peace. No wonder you're a fan! I like to come to this spot by the water near my mom's old house. It's where I reflect on her life and find some peace. Being surrounded by nature helps a lot.
[D4:34] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a small island with a lone boat in the water
[D4:35] Jolene: That's so touching! Do you have any little traditions that you do when you come to reflect on your mom?
[D4:36] Deborah: Do you remember this amulet from her? Whenever I come here, I bring it with me. It's how I feel her love and stay close to her. Holding it brings me comfort.
[D4:36] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman wearing a white shirt and a gold chain necklace
[D4:37] Jolene: It's amazing how something so small can have such a big impact, huh?
[D4:38] Deborah: Yeah, even small things like this can make a big difference. It's a reminder of all the love and strength we have inside, connecting us to people we've lost and comforting us.
[D4:39] Jolene: It can keep them close in our hearts every day.
[D4:40] Deborah: Anna also has a pendant that she wears in memory of her mother! This also brought us closer.
[D4:41] Jolene: It's nice to have those reminders as a source of strength when we need it.

[D5:13] Jolene: I'll keep you posted! Appreciate the support! Here are my sketches in the planner.
[D5:13] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a notebook with a pen and a notebook with a page of notes
[D5:14] Deborah: Sounds like you're doing great. Let me know if you need more tips or information.
[D5:15] Jolene: Thanks, Deb! If I need anything else, I'll let you know. You're awesome!
[D5:16] Deborah: You're awesome too! Take care!
[D5:17] Jolene: Stay safe!

[D27:8] Deborah: That's great, Jolene! Practicing mindfulness and gratitude can really change our day-to-day. Even just a different outlook can make the little things in life joyful. Glad you're getting into it!
[D27:9] Jolene: I'm experiencing a new level of joy and happiness!
[D27:10] Deborah:  It's wonderful to see your progress, and I'm excited to be on this journey with you!
[D27:11] Jolene: Thanks, Deb! Appreciate your support. It's great that we can do this together.
[D27:12] Deborah: Having a supportive community definitely helps. We can motivate and encourage each other! By the way, I recently played a game. I don't remember what it's called. This is a card game about cats, where you take cards one by one from a deck, and then you can attack your opponent with them. We'll definitely play it with you!

Session date: 4:50 pm on 25 February, 2023
[D7:16] Deborah:  Always rooting for you. Remember to listen to your heart and take good care. Here's a photo I took while reflecting outdoors. It's a reminder to find peace even in chaos.
[D7:16] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a person sitting on a bench looking at the sunset
[D7:17] Jolene:  I'm curious, what does your daily routine look like?
[D7:18] Deborah: In the morning, I meditate, do yoga, and teach classes. And yesterday I went for a morning jog for the first time in a nearby park. I will now incorporate this into my daily routine. And in the evenings, I spend time with loved ones.
[D7:19] Jolene: Why did you decide that?
[D7:20] Deborah: Exercise is key for me - it makes me feel connected to my body. 
[D7:21] Jolene: This is a great healthy habit!
[D7:22] Deborah: It's like they say - "Can't pour from an empty cup." Looking out for ourselves gives us the energy to help others. And don't forget, you're worth it too!
[D7:23] Jolene: Thanks, Deb. Your words really mean something to me. I'll keep remembering to prioritize self-care.
Session date: 7:18 pm on 2 March, 2023
[D8:1] Deborah: Hey Jolene, Anna got me a vegan stir-fry the other day - tofu and veg with ginger and soy sauce. It was really tasty! Food is such a wonderful source of pleasure and nourishment. What dishes are comforting to you?
[D8:2] Jolene: One of my favorite dishes is lasagna! Comfort food can be a great pick-me-up. I've got a lot going on with my studies and exams.
[D8:3] Deborah: Have you been able to find time for yourself lately?
[D8:4] Jolene: I've been trying to squeeze in some me-time. Last Friday, I did yoga and meditation to relax. Did you find time for yourself too?
[D8:4] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a room with a wooden floor and a window
[D8:5] Deborah:  I also did the same, it helped me reset my mind. How does it make you feel?
[D8:6] Jolene: It's amazing how a few quiet moments can work wonders for the soul.
[D8:6] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a purse with a plant on a table
[D8:7] Deborah: Have you been able to get outside lately?
[D8:8] Jolene: I did take Seraphim to the park last Sunday. She loved it and here's a pic.
[D8:8] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a lizard laying on the ground surrounded by leaves
[D8:9] Deborah: Looks like you guys had fun!
[D8:10] Jolene: We explored new places. People are surprised when they see a tamed snake. What do you like about being outdoors?
[D8:11] Deborah: Hmm... The birds chirping and the breeze gently blowing! It reminds me of what really matters.
[D8:12] Jolene: Yep, it's like a reminder to slow down and appreciate the little things.
[D8:13] Deborah: Is there anything you want to be more mindful of right now?
[D8:14] Jolene: I need to be more mindful of my stress levels and take care of my mental health. Sometimes I get too caught up in my studies and forget to prioritize self-care.
[D8:15] Deborah:  Life can get hectic and it's easy to forget about ourselves. 
[D8:16] Jolene: Exams and deadlines got me feeling overwhelmed. Just look at my to-do list! It seems never-ending... Trying my best but it's been challenging.
[D8:16] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a desk with a notebook and a computer monitor
[D8:17] Deborah: Your efforts will bear fruit, don't give up!
[D8:18] Jolene: Thanks, Deb. Any tips on studying or time management?
[D8:19] Deborah: My tip is to break it into smaller pieces and set goals for yourself. For time management, planners or schedulers help you stay organized and give you time for yourself. Let me know if you need help with a study plan!
[D8:20] Jolene: I appreciate your help with that.
[D8:21] Deborah: Take care and good luck with your exams. I'll give you a mug just like this one! It encourages.
[D8:21] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a yellow coffee cup with a handwritten message
[D8:22] Jolene: Thanks, Deb! This really cheered me up. All the best with your classes. Bye!
[D8:23] Deborah: Thanks, Jolene! Glad I could bring a smile to your face. Take care and make sure to give yourself some time to relax. Bye!
Session date: 11:22 am on 13 March, 2023
[D9:1] Deborah: Hi Jolene! We haven't corresponded for a long time!
[D9:2] Jolene: Hey Deb, yeah life can get chaotic. How's it been going lately?
[D9:3] Deborah: So much has been going on lately. I started this yoga class in the neighborhood - it's such a good feeling! Now I get to share the exercise with my neighbors and watch it really transform them.
[D9:4] Jolene:  Congrats. How did you do this?
[D9:5] Deborah: Thanks! My neighbors were interested in trying yoga, so I hosted a class for them on Friday. It was great to see everyone embrace and enjoy it. Here is our photo together.
[D9:5] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a group of women posing for a picture
[D9:6] Jolene: That's cool! What made you want to start teaching it?
[D9:7] Deborah: I find it calming and wanted to share that with others. Giving people peace and awareness brings me so much happiness.
[D9:8] Jolene: Wow, Deb! It's awesome when we can share something we love and make things better for others.
[D9:9] Deborah: Teaching it is awesome because it can help others and I've made such great friends through it. It's really nice for building community connections.
[D9:10] Jolene: That's really motivating. It's great to have support in tough times.
[D9:11] Deborah: It's one of life's best parts, right?
[D9:12] Jolene: Yeah, having someone to rely on is key in tough times. It really makes a difference in how we handle life. Plus, there's something I wanted to tell you.
[D9:13] Deborah: What's up? I'm listening. We'll figure it out.
[D9:14] Jolene: I'm having a hard time dealing with my Engineering assignments. It's a lot to manage and I'm struggling to keep up. Can we still talk about time management?
[D9:15] Deborah: Sure, Jolene. Let's find a time that works for both of us.
[D9:16] Jolene: Let's find a time to chat - I'll check my schedule and get back to you.
[D9:17] Deborah: Take your time, Jolene. We'll work it out. Take care of yourself, OK?
[D9:18] Jolene:  I'll make sure to take it. See you soon!
[D9:19] Deborah:  I'm here for you if you need me. Let's catch up soon.
[D9:20] Jolene: Have a great day!
Session date: 5:35 pm on 22 March, 2023
[D10:1] Deborah: Hey Jolene, it's been a while. Hope you're doing okay with all your exams and deadlines. I know it's difficult for you right now.
[D10:2] Jolene: Hey Deb! Yeah, it can be tough. Trying to find time for everything is like playing catch-up - really stressful!
[D10:3] Deborah:  How do you manage your time and stay organized with all the projects and deadlines?
[D10:4] Jolene: I'm using the Pomodoro Technique - 25 minutes work, 5-minute break - to avoid burnout but I'm still struggling to prioritize. Do you have any other tips on time management?
[D10:5] Deborah: I create a daily schedule or to-do list. Here's my example for today.
[D10:5] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a notepad with a list of things to do
[D10:6] Jolene: I tried making one but it's kinda overwhelming when it's a big stack of tasks. Here's an example from last Friday.
[D10:6] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a notepad with notes on it on a counter
